newsitem.title: GERMANY: Stoiber welcomes Kohl remark on meeting EMU goals.
newsitem.headline: Stoiber welcomes Kohl remark on meeting EMU goals.

text.p: Bavarian Premier Edmund Stoiber said on Tuesday he welcomed Chancellor Helmut Kohl's remark that the deficit rule for European monetary union would be met, but he added the debate over EMU would go on.
On Monday in Berlin, Kohl said the entry criterion of 3.0 percent (of gross domestic product) would not be watered down.
Speaking at an entrepreneurs' conference where Kohl was also present, Stoiber said the chancellor had expressed "with greatest clarity" that the convergence criteria would be met.

Stoiber, a rival of Finance Minister Theo Waigel's for leadership of the Christian Social Union (CSU), Bavarian sister party to Kohl's Christian Democratic Union (CDU), has been sniping at the coalition to ensure that the EMU criteria be strictly met.
At the conference, Stoiber said a stable euro would be a great opportunity for the German and the European economy.
Stoiber said he would not be meeting with Kohl personally to discuss the issue.
